newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Rainy days and Monday could get HK, UK and PRC down.
newsitem.headline: Rainy days and Monday could get HK, UK and PRC down.

text.p: It's likely to rain on Hong Kong's big parade. That's official.
Will the clouds part long enough for the sun to shine on the end of Britain's empire or will it be stormy Handover Blues?
Britain hands this tropical territory back to China next month, about the steamiest and wettest time of the year.
"Rainy days and Mondays always get me down," sang The Carpenters. Hong Kong faces both, a double whammy that could hit Asia's "Party of the Century."
The city's date with destiny is at midnight on Monday, June 30, fixed by the lapse of a 19th century pact.
Then, royal heir Prince Charles, representing the United Kingdom, presents to the People's Republic of China the territory seized from the old Manchu Dynasty by military force and "unequal treaties."
This ceremony will be indoors at the spectacular new harbourside Hong Kong Convention Centre, but lots of celebratory events are scheduled for outdoors.
These include a military parade, fireworks and a multi-million dollar extravaganza of decorated barges and giant balloons in the main harbour.

Hong Kong's Royal Observatory - soon to lose that imperial prefix - said in a statement on Friday: "Historically the chance of rain on June 30 or July 1 is 60 percent or higher. The rain could also be heavy."
Cyclones and typhoons which hit East Asia with demonic force are possible, too. They halt everything.
So it might be a rough, as well as a gloomy, farewell voyage when the royal yacht Britannia leaves harbour carrying Prince Charles and last governor Chris Patten.
The observatory avoided making a forecast at this stage, beyond saying a wide spectrum of weather is possible at that time.

But with a touch of British-style understatement, the announcement concluded: "In planning one's activities it would be prudent to take into consideration the possibility of inclement weather on those two days."
As another song goes, "Stormy weather, don't know why there's no sun up in the sky, stormy weather..."
